rules.quote: Use the heading ‘Notes’ for footnotes in digital content and for endnotes. Don’t use a heading for footnotes in print-only publications.
rules.violation_condition: using a heading other than 'Notes' for footnotes in digital content or endnotes, or including a heading for footnotes in a print-only publication
when: In digital content, footnotes take the heading 'Notes'.
Endnotes take the heading 'Notes'.
In print-only publications, footnotes do not take any heading.
rules.why: Clear instruction establishing heading rules for notes across media types.

covers.quote: Reference symbols are best for content with many numbers, such as content with mathematical equations.
Use symbols if there’s a risk that users will confuse superscript numbers for exponents.

examples.note: A reference symbol is used to avoid confusion with mathematical powers/exponents.
Using a superscript number can be confused with an exponent.

rules.quote: Use reference numbers instead of symbols in most content.
rules.specification: Use numbers as default; use symbols only when numbers would be confused with mathematical notations like exponents.
rules.violation_condition: using symbols for reference markers where numbers could be used without ambiguity or technical limitation
when: Use symbols if there is a risk of confusion with exponents or mathematical equations.
rules.why: G-2 consolidates the preference for numbers with the specific exception for mathematical content.

rules.quote: If you use symbols, use footnotes instead of endnotes.
rules.violation_condition: using endnotes rather than footnotes when reference markers are symbols
when: When symbols are chosen as reference markers.
rules.why: Direct formatting instruction coupling symbol markers to footnotes.

covers.quote: Restart the symbols on each page. If you have more than five notes on a page, double the symbols (**, ††).

rules.quote:
Use the symbols in this order:

* (asterisk)
† (dagger)
‡ (double dagger)
§ (section sign)
# (hash sign).
rules.violation_condition: introducing reference symbols in an order other than asterisk (*), dagger (†), double dagger (‡), section sign (§), and hash sign (#), or failing to double symbols after 5 notes on a page
when: When using symbols for reference markers on a page.
Restart the symbols on each page.
Double the symbols (**, ††) if there are more than 5 notes on a page.
rules.why: G-2 groups the fixed sequence of symbols and their overflow/restart rules into one rule.

rules.why: Specific grammatical placement rule for in-text reference markers.

rules.quote: Don’t use more than one reference marker in the same place, such as when citing 2 works. Instead cite both works in one footnote or endnote, separating the entries in the note with a semicolon.
rules.violation_condition: multiple adjacent reference markers (e.g. superscript comma-separated numbers) in the same place in the text
when: When citing two or more works at the same point in text, use one marker and separate entries in the note with a semicolon.
rules.why: Clear negative instruction against multiple adjacent reference markers.

rules.quote: Don’t use the Latin abbreviations ‘ibid.’, ‘op cit.’ or ‘loc cit.’ for repeated citations.

the letter ‘p’ and the page number to cite one page
the letters ‘pp’ and the page number range to cite a range of pages.

rules.quote: For tables and images (such as graphs) you’re using in the content, attribute the source in the notes below the table or image (also called a ‘figure’). when: When citing works accessed online (except online books published in set editions).
rules.why: G-2 and G-4 consolidate the general requirement for access dates across online references.

anchor.quote: If the PDF doesn’t have a landing page, link to the PDF and include ‘PDF’ in square brackets after the title. Follow ‘PDF’ with the file size in kilobytes (KB) or megabytes (MB). Include both of these additional details in the linked text.

examples.note: Format and file size included in brackets.

parts.quote: Thomson Reuters, Abbreviations guide [PDF 9 MB], Westlaw Advantage Australia, 2026, accessed 4 June 2026.

tags.violation_condition: linking directly to a PDF without '[PDF X KB/MB]' in the linked text after the title

when: When citing a PDF that has no landing page to link to.
rules.why: Defines format and size indicator requirements when directly linking a PDF.

anchor.quote: If the document has a DOI, include it in the citation. Put it at the end of the citation and include the shortened form ‘doi’ in lower case before it.

covers.quote: If you include a DOI, you don’t need to include a publishing location.

examples.note: Ends citation with lowercase 'doi:' followed by the identifier.

parts.quote: T Kelleher, ‘Conversational voice’,Journal of Communication, 2009, 59(1):172–188, doi:10.1111/j.1460-2466.2008.01410.x.

tags.violation_condition: capitalising 'DOI' or omitting the DOI when citing a document that has one, or placing it somewhere other than the end of the citation

when: When citing a document that has a DOI.
rules.why: Clear instruction on formatting and placement of DOIs in notes.

anchor.quote: If the citation has a volume number, an issue number and page numbers follow the format: volume(issue):page–page.

examples.note: Follows volume(issue):page-page format.

parts.quote: D Jackson, X Li and P Chandran, ‘Safety and equity’, Psychological Science Australia, 2018, 2(4):223–240.

tags.violation_condition: formatting journal volume, issue, and page numbers with spaces, 'vol.', 'no.', or letters instead of 'volume(issue):page–page'

when: When citing periodicals containing volume, issue, and page range.
rules.why: Specific pattern for periodical volume/issue/page citations.

anchor.quote: For tables and images (such as graphs) you’re using in the content, attribute the source in the notes below the table or image (also called a ‘figure’). Include permission or copyright information if necessary. Don’t include this information or a reference marker in the caption or title to the table or figure.

examples.note: Attribution placed below figure/table using 'Source:'.

parts.quote: Source: Adapted from Murray–Darling Basin Authority (MDBA), Annual report 2018–19, MDBA, Australian Government, 2019, accessed 3 February 2020.

tags.violation_condition: placing source attribution or a reference marker inside the caption or title of a table or figure instead of in the notes below it

when: When attributing a table or figure in content.
rules.why: Explicit negative rule forbidding attribution/markers in captions/titles of tables and figures.

anchor.quote: For emails and personal communication, mention them in the text but don’t include a note.

examples.note: Referenced in text, no note created.

parts.quote: Susannah Bishop (personal communication, 5 February 2020) wrote ...

tags.violation_condition: creating a footnote or endnote citation for an email or personal communication instead of mentioning it in the body text

when: When referencing emails or personal communication.
rules.why: Explicit instruction prohibiting notes for personal communications.

anchor.quote: For dictionaries and encyclopaedias, mention them in the text but don’t include a note.

examples.note: Cited directly in body text, no note created.

parts.quote: The Australian concise Oxford dictionary (ACOD) defines it as …

tags.violation_condition: creating a footnote or endnote citation for a dictionary or encyclopaedia instead of mentioning it in the body text

when: When referencing dictionaries or encyclopaedias.
rules.why: Explicit instruction prohibiting notes for dictionaries and encyclopaedias.
